title: Tensor and closed-adjunction consequences of coordinate scalar normalization
statement:
Let A be a finite commutative ring killed by a positive integer N invertible on a Noetherian scheme T. Let hI make the affine zero section Cartier. In the actual ordinary arrows [def-pur-coordinate-section-core-arrows, def-pur-coordinate-section-ordinary-arrows], assume the identity-normalized compact pushforward of its supported Kummer map followed by coordinate integration equals identity on A_T. Then CoprojectionNormalization [def-pur-coordinate-section-coprojection-arrows] holds: the unit orientation is invertible and on both the unit and each M_r=A_T(r)[2r] the canonical closed coprojection mate is invertible and identifies ordinaryOrientation with tensoring the unit orientation. For every r, the closed proper projection is invertible, ordinaryOrientation is invertible, its compact transpose is identity tensor the scalar map conjugated by the coefficient unitors, and its exceptional composite with CoordinateLine.comparison and exceptionalComposition is identity. The hypothesis is just the scalar equation; no twisted conclusion or pro-etale comparison is assumed.

The exact Lean statement is:

theorem coordinateSectionTensorTrace
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0) [IsNoetherian T]
    (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))) (hI : (sectionMap T).ker.IsInvertible)
    (hnorm : ((sectionComposition A T).inv.app (Etale.ordinaryFiniteUnit A T) ≫
    (compact A T).map (restrictedSupported A T N hN hA hT hI) ≫
      CoordinateLine.integration A N hA T hN hT = 𝟙 _)) :
    CoprojectionNormalization A T N hN hA hT hI ∧
    ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ hpf : IsIso (closedProjection A T
      (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r)),
    IsIso (ordinaryOrientation A T N hN hA hT hI
      (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) hpf) ∧
    ((sectionComposition A T).inv.app
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) ≫
      (compact A T).map (tensorSupported A T N hN hA hT hI
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) hpf) ≫
      (CoordinateLine.adjunction A N hA T hN hT).counit.app
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) =
      (Etale.derivedTensorSingleUnitIso
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r)).inv ≫
      ((Etale.ordinaryFiniteTensor A T).obj
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r)).map
          ((sectionComposition A T).inv.app (Etale.ordinaryFiniteUnit A T) ≫
            (compact A T).map (restrictedSupported A T N hN hA hT hI) ≫
            CoordinateLine.integration A N hA T hN hT) ≫
      (Etale.derivedTensorSingleUnitIso
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r)).hom) ∧
    (ordinaryOrientation A T N hN hA hT hI
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) hpf ≫
      (closedImage A T).rightAdjoint.map
        ((CoordinateLine.comparison A N hA T hN hT).hom.app
          (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r)) ≫
      (exceptionalComposition A T).hom.app
        (Etale.SectionLocalDualizingComparisons.tateObject A N hA T r) = 𝟙 _)

source.place: Rank-one supported Cartier normalization, even twists and finite etale-origin transport; expanded parent proof steps as specified below.

proof.text: Finite etale twist pullback gives rank-one flat root lines. Their powers and even shifts are invertible and finite Tor. Proper projection for the closed section makes closedProjection and closedTensorProjection isomorphisms on every Tate input, including the literal unit.

The mate of inverse closed projection followed by identity tensor the closed counit is coprojectionMate. Immersion twist identifies this mate as an isomorphism. Substitute the adjunct-counit equation to obtain the stated formula for ordinaryOrientation. The two adjunctions and the conjugate composition turn the scalar equation into the untwisted exceptional identity. Their comparison factors are isomorphisms, so cancellation makes unitOrientation invertible; its tensor and the coprojection mate make the twisted orientation invertible.

Apply naturality of the coefficient-first projection map to the supported arrow. The composition projection mate for ps=id identifies the two successive projections with the identity projection under sectionComposition. Use the actual coordinate adjunction counit formula. This gives identity tensor the scalar map with its unitors. Transposing with the two adjunct-counit identities gives the final exceptional identity. The shifts contribute (-1)^(2r*2)=1.
